changes: Weekday normalised: 'roja 2' = Monday (Persian rōz count, day 2); kept as_written in date.as_written
ce_approx refined: ŚS 1809 Māgha śukla falls in Jan/Feb 1888 CE (ŚS+78 = 1887 for the start of the year)
Padmanābha: confidence lowered to medium (gurupadmanābhaprasādā(t) is a formulaic invocation; probably the scribe's human teacher, but could be read as Viṣṇu Padmanābha)
Notes expanded: catalogue King Dravya Śāha (16th-c. Gorkha ruler) is anachronistic for 1888; reigning king then was Pṛthvī Vīra Vikrama Śāha, not named in colophon

notes: The catalogue gives King Dravya Śāha, but the colophon names no king. Dravya Śāha was a 16th-century king of Gorkha, so that field cannot be right for a copy dated ŚS 1809 (c. 1888 CE). The king reigning in 1888 was Pṛthvī Vīra Vikrama Śāha, and he is not mentioned either. ŚS 1809 + 78 = 1887, but Māgha śukla 10 of that year falls in January/February 1888 CE. 'roja 2' uses the Persian day-count, so the weekday is Monday. 'gurupadmanābhaprasādā(t)' most likely names the scribe's human teacher Padmanābha. It could also be a formulaic invocation of Viṣṇu Padmanābha, so the confidence is medium. The work is a Sauramata (astral) text, the Ratnadīpaka/Ratnadīpikā.
